message.reasoning:
We need to generate JUnit 4 test cases covering all methods in JsonSchemaFactory. Need to test builder, defaultMetaSchemaURI validation, checkVersion, normalizeMetaSchemaUri, isYaml, idMatchesSourceUri, getSchema with string, InputStream, URI, caching, etc. Since many dependencies (JsonMetaSchema, JsonSchema, ValidationContext, URIFactory etc.) are complex, we can use mocks (Mockito) to isolate. However we need to keep test code compileable without external libraries? Usually Maven includes dependencies. We can use Mockito for mocking. Provide tests that verify behavior like IllegalArgumentException when null parameters passed to builder.build, etc.

We can also create a simple JsonMetaSchema stub that returns a fixed URI and implements readId. However JsonMetaSchema is abstract? Not sure. In library, JsonMetaSchema likely has methods getUri(), readId(JsonNode). Could create a subclass for testing.

Simplify: Use real JsonSchemaFactory.getInstance for V4 which uses builder and adds default meta schema. Then test checkVersion mapping, normalizeMetaSchemaUri transformations (http to https). Also test isYaml detection with various URIs.

Test idMatchesSourceUri: need JsonMetaSchema with readId returning a string; we can use a stub subclass that extends JsonMetaSchema (if abstract). We'll need to import com.networknt.schema.* . Provide inner class TestMetaSchema extends JsonMetaSchema { ... }.

Also test findMetaSchemaForSchema via getSchema(String) with schema containing $schema field referencing a known meta schema URI; verify that correct meta schema is used.

But many internal methods are private; we can test via public methods.

Test caching: Use a mock URIFactory and URIFetcher that return a known InputStream, enable caching, call getSchema(uri) twice, ensure fetcher called only once. Use Mockito verify.

We'll need to construct builder with custom factories and fetcher.

Plan test class JsonSchemaFactoryTest.

Test cases:

1. testCheckVersionValid: for each enum value returns correct instance type (Version4 etc). Use instanceof.

2. testCheckVersionNullReturnsNull.

3. testCheckVersionUnsupported: passing null? Actually default case throws IllegalArgumentException. Use a dummy enum? Not possible. Could use reflection to pass null? Already covered.

4. testNormalizeMetaSchemaUriRewritesToHttps: input "http://example.com/schema" returns "https://example.com/schema". Also ensures fragment and query removed.

5. testNormalizeMetaSchemaUriInvalidThrowsException: pass "://bad" expecting JsonSchemaException.

6. testIsYamlTrueForYmlAndYamlExtensions: build factory with minimal required parameters (use builder with a dummy meta schema). For that we need a meta schema with known URI and readId stub. Provide custom builder: JsonSchemaFactory.Builder builder = new JsonSchemaFactory.Builder().defaultMetaSchemaURI("http://example.com/draft-07/schema").addMetaSchema(new TestMetaSchema("http://example.com/draft-07/schema")); Then build.

Then call private isYaml via reflection, or we can make a subclass exposing it. Simpler: use reflection to invoke isYaml method.

7. testIdMatchesSourceUriTrueAndFalse: Use reflection to invoke idMatchesSourceUri, provide stub meta schema.

8. testBuilderValidationThrowsIllegalArgumentException: Build with null mapper, null yamlMapper, empty defaultMetaSchemaURI, missing meta schema, etc. Use builder then set fields via reflection? Builder doesn't expose setting of objectMapper null directly; we can call builder.objectMapper(null) then build expecting IllegalArgumentException.

9. testGetSchemaFromStringValidJson: Provide simple schema string "{}". Expect non-null JsonSchema. Use default meta schema.

10. testGetSchemaFromStringInvalidJsonThrowsJsonSchemaException: Pass malformed JSON, expect JsonSchemaException.

11. testGetSchemaFromURIWithCaching: Use mock URIFactory that returns same URI, mock URIFetcher that returns InputStream of simple schema. Build factory with enableUriSchemaCache(true). Call getSchema(uri) twice. Verify fetch called once.

12. testGetSchemaFromURICacheDisabled: Build with enableUriSchemaCache(false). Verify fetch called twice.

Will need to import com.networknt.schema.*, Jackson, JUnit, Mockito.

Provide static inner class TestMetaSchema extends JsonMetaSchema. We need to implement abstract methods: getUri(), readId(JsonNode). Looking at library, JsonMetaSchema likely has many methods; but for our test we only need getUri() and readId(). However subclass may need to implement many abstract methods. Could instead use a mock JsonMetaSchema via Mockito. That's easier: Mockito.mock(JsonMetaSchema.class). Set behavior for getUri() and readId(). However builder.addMetaSchema expects a JsonMetaSchema; we can add mock.

Thus we can create mockMetaSchema = mock(JsonMetaSchema.class); when(mockMetaSchema.getUri()).thenReturn("http://example.com/draft-07/schema"); when(mockMetaSchema.readId(any())).thenReturn(null). Then builder.addMetaSchema(mockMetaSchema). That may be sufficient.

Now test builder validation: builder.objectMapper(null) .defaultMetaSchemaURI("http://example.com/draft-07/schema") .addMetaSchema(mockMetaSchema).build() should throw IllegalArgumentException.

Similarly test yamlMapper null.

Now writing tests.

Need to handle reflection for private methods isYaml and idMatchesSourceUri. Use Method method = JsonSchemaFactory.class.getDeclaredMethod("isYaml", URI.class); method.setAccessible(true); boolean result = (Boolean) method.invoke(factory, uri);

Similarly for idMatchesSourceUri.

Now produce final output with markers.
